key_insight: The paper shows how to turn standard neural architectures into neural operators that work directly on continuous function spaces, rather than on fixed grids. This makes learned scientific models much less sensitive to how the data are discretized.
problem_solved: Many neural networks perform well only at the resolution they were trained on, so predictions can break when the grid, mesh, or sampling of scientific data changes. The paper addresses the need for discretization-agnostic models that generalize across resolutions.
method: Extend popular neural network architectures into function-space operators that accept continuous inputs and outputs.
Design principled adaptations so the resulting models can learn from scientific data without depending on a specific discretization.
Enable operator learning that transfers more reliably across meshes, grids, and sampling resolutions.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners working in scientific computing, this offers a more robust path to building surrogate models and simulators that generalize beyond the training resolution. It can improve portability, reduce retraining needs, and make neural models more useful for real-world physics and engineering tasks.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram comparing a standard grid-based neural network vs. a discretization-agnostic neural operator

Icons representing physics simulation, differential equations, and scientific data
paper_title: Principled approaches for extending neural architectures to function spaces for operator learning
paper_authors: Julius Berner, Miguel Liu-Schiaffini, Jean Kossaifi, Valentin Duruisseaux, Boris Bonev
